issues.explanation: The PRD-original ACs (AC-FR-1-a/b/c, AC-FR-2-a/b/c, AC-FR-3-a/b/c, AC-FR-4a-a..d, AC-FR-4b-a..d, AC-FR-4c-a..d, AC-FR-5-a/b/c, AC-FR-6-a, AC-FR-7-a) are formally defined in prd-v1.md lines 119-190 and are inherited by the Blueprint via 'see PRD §FR-N' references in its Functional Requirements section. The Blueprint then expands each into AC-CC-N-x / AC-CS-Nx-y / AC-CICD-N-x. The Plan tags each task with BOTH the PRD-original ID and the Blueprint-expanded IDs as aliases. The Acceptance Tests coverage matrix only enumerates Blueprint-expanded IDs, so a reader looking up 'AC-FR-4a-a' will not find a row — they would have to follow the alias to AC-CS-4a-1. The mapping is recoverable from the Plan's cross-reference table, but the matrix should state the alias relationship explicitly.
issues.recommended_resolution: Add a one-line preamble to the Acceptance Tests Coverage Matrix stating: 'PRD-original AC-FR-N-x IDs are treated as aliases for their Blueprint-expanded forms (AC-CC-N-x for Claude-Code-layer FRs, AC-CS-Nx-y for Codespaces FRs, AC-CICD-N-x for CI/CD FRs); the matrix indexes by the expanded form only.' Or alternatively add a small alias table at the top of the matrix. No test re-authoring required.

issues.summary: Blueprint v2.2 enumerates AC-NFR-14 and AC-NFR-15 inline but does not lift AC-NFR-1-a through AC-NFR-13-b into its own AC catalog; downstream artifacts (Plan + Tests) cite these IDs as if they were Blueprint-local.

evidence.section: §Non-Functional Requirements lines 340-407 — the canonical AC-NFR-1-a through AC-NFR-13-b definitions

§Acceptance Criteria — only AC-NFR-14 and AC-NFR-15 are enumerated inline (lines 501-504); AC-NFR-1-a..AC-NFR-13-b are inherited-by-reference via the Functional Requirements references 'see PRD §FR-N'
Acceptance Test Cross-Reference §Non-Functional ACs lines 779-795 — cites AC-NFR-1-a/2-a/3-a/3-b/4-a/4-b/5-a/6-a/7-a/8-a/9-a/10-a/11-a/13-a/13-b/14/15
§Coverage Matrix lines 130-145 — same IDs cited

issues.explanation: The v2.2 amendment's stated purpose (per change_summary) was to lift the 18 per-layer-design ACs into the Blueprint's canonical AC catalog so every Plan/Test citation resolves to a Blueprint-local definition. That purpose was honored for AC-CC-* / AC-CS-* / AC-CICD-* / AC-NFR-14 / AC-NFR-15. But AC-NFR-1-a..AC-NFR-13-b are still inherited-by-reference from the PRD rather than enumerated inline. This is consistent with the inheritance convention (the FRs themselves also work this way: 'see PRD §FR-N') and may be intentional, but it is an asymmetry from the AC-lift-cycle's nominal goal. A reader of Blueprint v2.2 alone, looking for AC-NFR-7-a, will not find it inline; they must traverse to prd-v1.md §NFR-7 line 371. The Plan and Tests treat these as Blueprint-local citations.
issues.recommended_resolution: One of: (a) add a one-line note at the head of the Blueprint's §Acceptance Criteria stating 'AC-NFR-1-a through AC-NFR-13-b inherit verbatim from prd-v1.md §Non-Functional Requirements lines 340-407; they are not re-stated inline'; (b) lift the AC-NFR-1-a..AC-NFR-13-b bullets into the Blueprint catalog inline (mirrors the v2.2 lift discipline more strictly); or (c) accept the current asymmetric inheritance as deliberate and document the rationale in the Blueprint's change_summary or §Acceptance Criteria preamble. Option (a) is the lowest-cost path.

The v2.2 lift was triggered by Plan reconciliation finding I-DR-002 (Plan tasks T2.x/T3.x/T4.x/T7.x cited AC IDs the Blueprint declared 'see Blueprint v1'). The Plan and Validators were authored against v2.1; the Tests were aligned to v2.2 post-lift. The Plan and Validators now read older-than-Blueprint, which is a normal sequencing artifact during reconciliation cycles but should be reconciled before final approval. The substance is unchanged — v2.2 is purely additive lift of AC definitions per the change_summary — so the version-pointer update is the load-bearing fix, not any re-authoring.
issues.recommended_resolution: Update Plan v1.0.1 → v1.0.2 (or in-place patch) replacing 'Blueprint v2.1' references with 'Blueprint v2.2' in §Source line 62 and §Purpose line 54 and revision_history. Same change to phase-validators.md §Source line 39 and §Conventions/related sections that cite 'Blueprint v2.1'. This is a frontmatter / pointer-update edit — no task content shifts. Sequencing risk: if Plan re-runs through plan-author the version-bump should not regenerate the document; a small mechanical sed-style edit by finalize-reconciler is the right shape.

issues.summary: Plan revision_history v1.0.0 entry still says '47 tasks' even though v1.0.1 corrected the total to 36; the v1.0.0 historical row should remain as a record of the prior state but is in the same Update History table as v1.0.1 without flagging that the 47 was corrected.

evidence.section: §Update History line 848 — '1.0.0 ... 47 tasks; single bundled PR per D-0008'
frontmatter total_tasks: 36 (line 8) and revision_history v1.0.1 edits[0]: 'I-DR-001 — corrected task count 47 → 36' (line 18)

issues.explanation: The Update History table at line 848 records Plan v1.0.0's task count as 47, which was the counter error that I-DR-001 later corrected. The v1.0.1 revision_history correctly documents the correction, but a reader of §Update History alone will see two different totals (47 in the v1.0.0 row, 36 in everything else) without an inline note connecting them. This is a minor consistency issue — the correction is documented elsewhere — but the Update History should record the actual final state (36) or flag the historical 47 as 'counter error — see v1.0.1'.
issues.recommended_resolution: Either (a) update the v1.0.0 row in Update History to say '36 tasks (originally counted as 47; corrected in v1.0.1 per I-DR-001)' — honest amendment of the historical record; or (b) leave v1.0.0 row verbatim (since revision_history v1.0.1 already documents the correction) and accept the minor inconsistency. Option (a) is cheap and removes the cross-row reader friction.

issues.summary: Acceptance Tests §Open Coverage Gaps item 7 surfaces a SHA-pinning symmetry gap (no AT explicitly diffs the two workflows' uses: lines); Phase Validator PV-3 also covers SHA-pin checks but only verifies each workflow declares pins, not that they match each other.

evidence.section: §Open Coverage Gaps item 7 lines 1381 — 'No AC explicitly tests the symmetric SHA-pinning commitment across both workflows. The Blueprint requires SHA-pinning is identical for actions/checkout and devcontainers/ci in FR-5 and FR-4c. AT-052 and AT-062 inspect each workflow's permissions and credentials but do not assert pin equality between the two YAMLs. Suggested follow-up: add a static-inspection check that grep-diffs the two workflows' uses: lines.'

PV-3.C1 lines 353 and PV-3.C2 lines 360 — each asserts SHAs in each workflow match PV-0.C2; §Operational checks line 394 'FR-5 and FR-4c cite the SAME SHA for actions/checkout and the SAME SHA for devcontainers/ci ... verified by SHA string-comparison across both files'
T0.2 'Both workflows (FR-5 and FR-4c) MUST use the same resolved SHA for each action — one resolution effort per action, two reuses'

issues.explanation: The Plan and Validators DO cover the cross-workflow SHA equality (PV-3 §Operational checks line 394). The Acceptance Tests authored AT-052 (FR-4c permissions/secrets) and AT-062 (FR-5 permissions/secrets) but flagged in Open Coverage Gaps item 7 that no AT explicitly diffs the two YAMLs' uses: lines. So this gap is between Tests (no explicit AT) and Validators (implicit via PV-3 op-check) — the check exists in the validator surface but not as a discrete test. Not blocking; the validator covers it.
issues.recommended_resolution: Either (a) author a follow-up AT (e.g., AT-080) that asserts the two workflow YAMLs' uses: SHA values are byte-identical for actions/checkout and for devcontainers/ci — small static-inspection test, ~10 lines; or (b) accept that PV-3 §Operational checks already covers this and update the Tests §Open Coverage Gaps item 7 to reference PV-3 as the existing coverage path. issues.summary: Plan Phase 5 lists 4 tasks (T5.1 through T5.4); the dispatch prompt notes 'T5.2 is the terminal write-action of the run; T5.3 and T5.4 are post-action observation tasks'. Phase Validator PV-5 has 4 criteria (C1-C4) but PV-5.C4 (post-launch observation log) is given MAJOR severity, which is inconsistent with the rest of PV-5's BLOCKER posture and with the Plan's framing of T5.4 as 'open-ended observation'.

evidence.section: T5.4 lines 557-566 — 'Estimate: S (ongoing observation over the first weeks post-merge)'; 'Satisfies AC: PRD §Success Criteria quantitative + qualitative metrics; AC-NFR-5-a (determinism — confirmed by observing no flakes)'

BLOCKER if a kill-criteria trigger has fired and is not yet acted on per the PRD's kill-criteria procedure.'

§Phase 5 Goal preamble line 520 — 'T5.2 is the terminal write-action of the run; T5.3 and T5.4 are post-action observation tasks that watch for the first cron-tick and capture post-launch evidence against PRD §Success Criteria.'

issues.explanation: PV-5.C4's compound severity ('MAJOR for log existence; BLOCKER if kill-criterion fires') is correct given T5.4's ongoing nature — the validator cannot demand full coverage of an open-ended observation window. The cross-artifact reader needs to know this is intentional rather than an oversight. The Plan's framing supports the validator's compound severity, but a one-line acknowledgement in the validator would close the loop.
issues.recommended_resolution: Add a one-line note to PV-5.C4 cross-referencing Plan T5.4's open-ended observation framing: 'PV-5.C4's compound severity reflects T5.4's open-ended observation window; full-coverage MAJOR is acceptable at PV-5 boundary because completeness can extend beyond it.' convergence.notes: First Cross-Artifact Audit round for this feature. No prior audit JSON to compare. Convergence baseline established here for rounds 2..4 if invoked.

summary.note: Per KB-review-disciplines severity taxonomy: 0 critical, 5 important, 3 recommended. Reported under both the BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR convention (where BLOCKER = critical, MAJOR = important, MINOR = recommended) and the critical/important/recommended convention so the orchestrator may consume either.

verdict_rationale: No critical/BLOCKER issues. 5 important issues are all surface-level consistency or completeness gaps (PRD-original AC ID alias note missing from Tests matrix; AC-NFR inheritance asymmetry; Plan/Validators still reference Blueprint v2.1 in source pointers; Plan Update History row v1.0.0 records pre-correction task count; Plan OI-1 stale-resolution wording). Each has a low-cost mechanical fix. 3 recommended issues are polish (validators-to-AT cross-reference, cross-workflow SHA equality test, PV-5.C4 compound-severity explanation). Per KB-review-disciplines severity taxonomy threshold mapping: no critical → not needs_revision; important present (small count) AND consistency / completeness implicitly > 80 / > 75 → approved_with_conditions / conditional_pass. The substantive cross-artifact alignment is sound: AC-lift cycle accomplished its stated purpose (C-PASS-001); AT coverage is exhaustive in both directions (C-PASS-002, C-PASS-003); PV-N exit criteria align with Plan phase exits (C-PASS-004); NFR thresholds concrete and verifiable (C-PASS-005); carve-out boundary preserved (C-PASS-006); v2.1 reconciliation findings (I-AA-001, I-AA-002, I-AA-003) propagated cleanly through downstream artifacts (C-PASS-007, C-PASS-008, C-PASS-009); FR-4 family three-sub-mechanism split consistent (C-PASS-010); single-bundled-PR posture preserved (C-PASS-012).
diff_mode_caveats: This audit operated under diff-mode discipline per ADR-0009: the auditor consumed the blueprint-diff-v2.patch (2016 lines) + Blueprint v2.2 changed sections (read in full) + Plan v1.0.1 in full + Acceptance Tests v1.0.0 in full + Phase Validators v1.0.0 in full.
